briefs.title: The Chain Rule
briefs.what_it_is: The Chain Rule is the Differentiation: Composite, Implicit, and Inverse Functions topic where you turn the concept into an AP-ready action: identify the outer and inner functions and multiply by the derivative of the inside.
briefs.why_it_matters: It matters because Unit 3 questions often award credit for connecting the model, representation, formula, or condition to a clear conclusion in context, not just for naming the topic.
briefs.how_points_are_earned: Points are earned when you identify the outer and inner functions and multiply by the derivative of the inside, show the required setup or condition check, and state the result in the language of the prompt.
briefs.answer_move: First name the quantity, structure, condition, or representation the prompt is really asking about; then identify the outer and inner functions and multiply by the derivative of the inside before doing arithmetic or writing the final sentence.
briefs.common_point_loss: Differentiating the outside correctly but forgetting the inner derivative

briefs.title: Implicit Differentiation

briefs.why_it_matters: It matters because Unit 3 questions often award credit for connecting the model, representation, formula, or condition to a clear conclusion in context, not just for naming the topic.
briefs.how_points_are_earned: Points are earned when you differentiate both sides with respect to x, attach dy/dx to every y-term, and solve for dy/dx when needed, show the required setup or condition check, and state the result in the language of the prompt.
briefs.answer_move: First name the quantity, structure, condition, or representation the prompt is really asking about; then differentiate both sides with respect to x, attach dy/dx to every y-term, and solve for dy/dx when needed before doing arithmetic or writing the final sentence.
